subject: Sorry about this morning
text:
Hi,

I'm really sorry about this morning, I didn't mean to leave you waiting outside the hall or to send you running between doors when the whole thing was my fault. I checked the event sheet twice, but I still grabbed the wrong volunteer bag and thought the spare parking pass was inside it, when in reality it was buried under the laundry I never folded last night. I should have texted you sooner instead of racing around trying to fix it myself, because I know how hard you were working to keep everything tidy while I was making excuses. I kept picturing the clock and kept telling myself one more minute, then one more, until it became too embarrassing to explain properly. Honestly, the mess was mine from start to finish, and your patience deserved a clearer answer long ago.

The practical concern now is the evening session, since the hall will already be full and the overflow room only opens if someone with organizer access signs the door. If we can't locate the pass by six, please don't let anyone park along the service road; last month they were towed, and I hate to think what that would cost you. Could you bring the folder from my desk? The blue key might be inside, and if not, I'll ask the library desk to hold the gate code until after cleanup. I'll meet you by the vending machines rather than stand you up again. I feel awful for making a simple swap into a scramble.
